---
title: "Theme tokens"
subtitle: "The vocabulary a theme is written in, and what each name accepts."
description: "The theme token vocabulary Lanterne validates against, its defaults, and the two reserved namespaces."
---

A theme is a flat dictionary of tokens.
`theme-tokens` returns the canonical defaults with named overrides applied, and `theme-merge` merges a dictionary of overrides into a complete one.
Both validate every key they touch, so an unknown token name or a value of the wrong type fails where it is written rather than where it is read.

```typst
#let base = theme-tokens(bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"), fg: rgb("#1c1c22"))
#let dark = theme-merge(base, (bg: rgb("#1c1c22"), fg: white))
```

## The vocabulary

Read from `src/theme/tokens.typ`.
The colour, typography and geometry groupings are documentation rather than structure: the dictionary is flat, so a theme merges without recursion and a generated theme is one dictionary literal.

| Token | Accepts | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg` | colour | `white` | The page fill. |
| `fg` | colour | `rgb("#111111")` | The text colour. |
| `accent` | colour | `rgb("#1f5fa9")` | The theme's accent, such as a title band's fill. |
| `accent-fg` | colour | `white` | The text colour on an accent fill. |
| `muted` | colour | `rgb("#6b6b76")` | Secondary text, such as a footer. |
| `border` | colour | `rgb("#d8d8e0")` | Rules and separators. |
| `dim-opacity` | ratio from 0% to 100% | `30%` | The text fill opacity a dimmed region renders at, read by `dim` and `focus`. |
| `font-base` | family name, coverage-scoped entry, or a non-empty array of them | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The body font. |
| `font-heading` | as `font-base` | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The heading font. |
| `size-base` | positive absolute length | `24pt` | The body text size. An `em` value is rejected here, since it would be relative to itself. |
| `scale-ratio` | number of at least 1 | `1.2` | The step between heading sizes, and what `smaller` divides by. |
| `weight-heading` | integer from 100 to 900, or a weight name | `"semibold"` | The heading weight. |
| `leading` | length | `0.75em` | The paragraph leading. |
| `margin` | length | `2cm` | The page margin. |
| `gutter` | non-negative length | `0.6cm` | The space between the regions of a slide. |
| `header-height` | non-negative length | `2cm` | The height of a header region. |
| `footer-height` | non-negative length | `1cm` | The height of a footer region. |
| `stroke-width` | non-negative length | `1pt` | The thickness of a rule or a border. |
| `extra` | dictionary | `(:)` | Tokens of your own. The one key whose contents are not validated. |
| `slots` | dictionary | `(:)` | A theme's renderers, validated against the five slot names. Nothing calls them yet. |

: The token vocabulary. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,25,15,45]"}

The named weights are `thin`, `extralight`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `extrabold` and `black`.

A non-negative length may carry an absolute part, a relative part, or both, and each part must be non-negative on its own.
That is stricter than it sounds: `2cm - 1em` is refused, although it resolves to a positive length at every plausible font size.
The two parts are read separately because Typst refuses to compare a mixed length with zero at all, and comparing the whole would replace this message with Typst's own.

The vocabulary grows with the code that reads a token.
The specification names twenty-eight, and the eighteen above are those the package validates today.
Ten of them are read now: `bg`, `fg`, `dim-opacity`, `font-base`, `font-heading`, `size-base`, `scale-ratio`, `weight-heading`, `leading` and `margin`.
The other eight are read by the renderer slots, which arrive in a later release, and the remaining names of the specification arrive with the layout and element milestones.

The six colour tokens are a matched set, tuned for the light default.
Each is overridden on its own, so a theme that sets `bg` to a dark fill should set `muted` and `border` as well, or the secondary text and the rules fall below a readable contrast.

## Heading sizes

A heading's size is `size-base` multiplied by `scale-ratio` raised to `max(0, 3 - level)`, so a section title reads as larger than a slide title and both read as larger than the body, and level 3 and below sit at the base size.

On a slide set `smaller`, the base of that calculation is the slide's own reduced size, so the title shrinks with the body rather than staying as large on the slide that asked for room.

## The `extra` namespace

`extra` exists so that a token of your own has somewhere to live.
The strictness everywhere else is the point: a mistyped token name that is quietly ignored is how a theme rots.

`extra` merges key by key rather than replacing wholesale, so setting one token of your own leaves the rest of the base theme's in place.
It is not itself a token name, so `theme-tokens(extra: ...)` is accepted as a key while an unknown name inside the vocabulary is refused.

## The `slots` namespace

::: {.callout-important}

## Not active yet

A theme carries slots today and nothing calls them.
The renderers arrive with the release that composes a page from regions.
Until then a slot is validated when you write it, and every slide renders exactly as it does without one.
:::

`slots` holds a theme's renderers.
It is the second reserved key, and like `extra` it is not a token name and merges key by key, so overriding one colour of a theme does not drop the renderers it supplied.

Unlike `extra`, its contents are validated.
A key must be one of `render-title-slide`, `render-section-slide`, `render-header`, `render-footer` or `render-progress`.
The set of five is fixed, and expanding it is a deliberate versioned decision.
A name outside it is refused rather than stored, because the renderer calls the five it knows and a sixth would be a function nothing ever runs.

Each slot is called with the named arguments `info`, `tokens` and `state`, and returns content.
Write all three, even where the slot ignores one.
Typst exposes nothing of a closure's parameters, so a slot's arity cannot be validated when you write it: one that does not accept all three fails when a page is composed, with Typst's own message rather than this package's.

```typst
#let banded = theme-tokens(
  accent: rgb("#1f5fa9"),
  slots: (render-header: (info: none, tokens: none, state: none) => []),
)
```

A value of `none` clears a slot rather than storing one.
That is how a theme takes another's chrome without one of its parts, since every other value has to be a function.

```typst
#let quiet = theme-merge(banded, (slots: (render-header: none)))
```
